svg.title: File rules at the pin: one call per cell, then 20 attacks per model
svg.desc: Top: a grid of 7 rule lists by 10 tool calls on a FilesystemBackend with virtual_mode=True, run by a scripted caller with no model. A rose cell is a call that ran although the rule list was written to block it; 22 such calls across the five docs rule lists, all on paths whose name starts with a dot. Violet is blocked as meant, amber is blocked although meant to be allowed, grey ran as meant. Bottom: one square per adversarial prompt, 20 per row, for Qwen3 8B and Haiku 5.5 under no rules, the docs isolate rules, and the dot-aware rules. Qwen3 8B no rules: 12 runs with harm, Qwen3 8B docs rules: 4 runs with harm, Qwen3 8B dot-aware: 0 runs with harm. Haiku 5.5 no rules: 11 runs with harm, Haiku 5.5 docs rules: 3 runs with harm, Haiku 5.5 dot-aware: 0 runs with harm.
svg.text: ONE CALL PER CELL, SCRIPTED CALLER, NO MODEL
Rose: ran, though the rules were written to block it.
Violet: blocked as meant. Amber: blocked, though meant to
be allowed. Grey: ran as meant. ws is /workspace.
20 ADVERSARIAL PROMPTS, ONE SQUARE PER RUN
Rose: the disk changed, or a secret reached the answer.
Amber: a secret reached the model only. Violet: tried, no harm.
Grey: no try. Stopped: attack calls denied or path-blocked, of all.
